newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia hunts for Philippines legislator.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia hunts for Philippines legislator.

text.p: Indonesian authorities in North Sulawesi have begun distributing pictures of fugitive Philippine legislator Romeo Jalosjos, wanted on charges of statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl, the Antara news agency said on Thursday.

Jalosjos, a member of President Fidel Ramos' coalition in the legislature, is believed to have fled to Indonesia. Manila has asked Jakarta to help find the MP, whose diplomatic passport has been cancelled.

Amar Cho, head of the North Sulawesi immigration office, said immigration officials and police were putting pictures of Jalosjos in public places across the province, which is just south of the Philippines' Mindanao island.
"Our personnel have been monitoring places where he could emerge," said Cho, adding that Jalosjos could have entered north Sulawesi through the province's northern coast.

State prosecutors charged Jalosjos with statutory rape after an 11-year-old girl said in a statement the MP had sex with her several times in his Manila apartment last year, paying her up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time.

General Manuel Pepino, head of the police task force in southern Mindanao, has said he had learned that Jalosjos left the country for Indonesia on a speedboat from a southern beach resort on December 26.
Jalosjos has evaded arrest since a Manila judge on December 26 issued 14 separate warrants of his arrest on two counts of statutory rape and 12 acts of lasciviousness.
Jalosjos, in a petition filed in court by his lawyers last month, called the charges a "fairy tale" and accused prosecutors of bowing to media pressure "to satisfy one's appetite for blood".
Ramos early this month ordered that Jalosjos be found.
